goal: Repair the three live worker queries still reading the users.business_id column dropped by migration 034, bound the OnboardingDripScheduler's unbounded re-queue of failed Outbox jobs, cap drips that are overdue past a grace window, and make a BullMQ handler's terminal error durably visible as a real Sentry issue instead of the breadcrumb nobody reads. Sentry ONLY — the sink deliberately writes no job_outbox.last_error, because the Watchdog's terminalizer overwrites it unconditionally with the very generic reclaim text the write existed to replace (deviations D3; the observability bullets below state the same).
non_goals: No migration and no schema change — the schema is already correct; the code is wrong
No CI static audit that diffs SQL column references against the migration-head schema — weighed and declined as its own epic-sized ticket; a live-DB suite covers this feature's queries
Not deleting, purging, or re-driving the 93 failed staging onboarding_drip rows — they are terminal and inert and stay as before/after evidence
Not changing the Watchdog state machine, its 15-minute stale window, or job_outbox.max_attempts — the job-failure sink records the error and deliberately does NOT terminalize the row
Not changing any BullMQ per-queue attempts or backoff configuration
Not changing WeeklySummaryWorker or MonthlyImpactWorker logic beyond consuming the fixed shared helper
Not re-firing drips that fall outside the staleness grace window — a drip skipped as too-late is skipped permanently, by design
No new env var and no new feature flag
user_visible_behavior: An entitled (Full access) location whose day_1 due date is inside the staleness grace window receives the day_1 onboarding drip email; today it receives nothing
day_7 and day_30 drips likewise send instead of throwing
WeeklySummaryWorker and MonthlyImpactWorker stop throwing 42703 the first time they run for a location — their dashboard-URL block resolves instead of aborting the whole report
The day_30 email's sign-off resolves only from businesses.onboarded_by; the business-scoped-admin sign-off is removed and day_30 renders with no sign-off where no onboarder exists
A drip whose due date passed more than the staleness grace window ago is never sent — no late welcome burst after an outage
No owner-facing surface, route, or template changes
invariants: Invariant #1 — all work stays on the Railway worker; no Next.js runtime import changes
Invariant #11 — drip entitlement keeps gating on subscriptionGrantsFullAccess, never a raw status literal
Invariant #15 — ownerHasDashboardAuth keeps taking sql as an explicit parameter; the new outbox helper does too. Only composition roots import the singleton
Invariant #12 — the job-failure sink is a named module (worker/job-failure-sink.ts), not an inline branch grown inside worker/index.ts
Invariant #2 — the job_outbox in-flight status vocabulary is untouched; the sink writes last_error only and never a status

The Watchdog remains the sole owner of the job_outbox status machine: the job-failure sink's UPDATE is guarded on status = 'dispatched' AND the dispatched outbox_attempt, so a domain 'failed' hook that already terminalized the row keeps its own last_error
Tenant scope: every touched query stays scoped by business_id or account_id and passes ci:tenant-scope
onboarding_drip stays idempotent — the three-way claim on onboarding_drip_log is unchanged and still precedes every side effect
edge_cases: A location whose owner row has auth_id IS NULL — dashboardUrl must be null, not a broken link, and the drip still sends
A location with no owner user row at all — same as above, no throw

An account with more than one business (multi-location): the rewritten owner lookup joins users -> accounts -> businesses, so it must match the owner of THAT location's account and not leak across accounts
A drip whose 3 failures are exactly 24 hours old — boundary of the rolling churn window
A drip with 2 failures in the last 24h — must still be re-queued
A drip exactly at the staleness grace boundary — must still send at the boundary and be skipped past it
day_7/day_30 for a location with subscription_activated_at NULL — existing markOutboxFailed path is unchanged and must stay unchanged
A BullMQ job that fails on an intermediate attempt and succeeds on retry — the sink must capture nothing and write nothing
A queue that already owns a domain 'failed' hook (publisher, zernio ingest, judge, csv ingest, solicitation batch, generate asks) — the generic sink must not stomp the domain hook's last_error
A job whose payload carries no outbox_id (hand-enqueued / legacy) — the sink must no-op rather than write against a BullMQ job id
The sink's own write failing — must be log-and-swallow, never allowed to escalate out of the 'failed' listener

worker/emitter-errors.ts — the precedent for a small named worker-level module attached to every queue in a loop from worker/index.ts
src/lib/shared/outbox.ts markOutboxCompleted/markOutboxFailed — the attempt-guarded UPDATE shape and the log-and-swallow-on-0-rows convention the new recordOutboxLastError follows
worker/background/schedulers/OnboardingDripScheduler.ts:43-54 — the existing NOT EXISTS due-drip predicate the two new bounds extend in place
src/lib/reviews/__tests__/*.integration.test.ts and assertSchemaReady — the live-DB suite convention (named *.integration.test.ts, no run-time DDL, provisioned by pnpm test:db:setup)

estimated_prod_lines: ±120 production lines changed, net NEGATIVE outside the one new module: the drip worker sheds its duplicated owner-auth query and a dead admin branch, and two existing outbox helpers (recordOutboxTransientError, isTerminalAttempt) are reused rather than reinvented.
estimated_test_lines: ±800 test lines across three suites (two live-DB, one unit). Raised from ±500 after the round-1 plan review found ten ways the 16-test eval could pass while the feature stayed wrong; the eval is now 25 tests. Unit mocks structurally cannot catch a dropped column, so live-DB coverage is the guard and test:prod of ~6:1 is correct here, not bloat (#643 lesson).
rollback_plan: Revert the PR. No migration, no schema change, no env var, no feature flag — every change is a query predicate, a deleted dead branch, or an additive failure-reporting module. Reverting restores the pre-fix behavior exactly (drips resume failing, churn resumes). The job-failure sink is additive and independently revertable by dropping the attachJobFailureSink call in worker/index.ts.
observability: A NEW job_outbox row with topic='onboarding_drip' reaches status='completed' on staging — the topic has never once done this; it is the single proof that defect A is fixed
A notification_deliveries row appears with template='onboarding_drip_day_1' and a Resend external_message_id
onboarding_drip_log.sent_at goes non-NULL for the claimed row
Worker log line: [OnboardingDripWorker] day_1 sent for business <id>
Scheduler log line naming the count of (business, drip_type) pairs skipped by the churn cap and by the staleness cap — a silently-skipped drip must not be indistinguishable from no drip being due

Sentry issue (not a breadcrumb) with tags {queue, topic} carrying the real handler error text on final BullMQ attempt — proven by the sink's unit tests, and the reason a future instance of this class surfaces in hours rather than months

job_outbox.last_error on a terminal row deliberately still reads the Watchdog reclaim text — the sink does NOT write it (the watchdog overwrites it unconditionally at OutboxPoller.ts:140-143, and raw messages can carry contact PII). Sentry is the single durable record of a handler error; CONTEXT.md and lab notes say so explicitly.
